title: North Carolina Family bought 600 acres in 1811; 214 years later, 298 acres protected from development
summary_full: In a remarkable effort to maintain their agricultural heritage, a North Carolina family has successfully preserved 298 acres of land from development over seven generations. Acquired in 1811 by John W. Caldwell and Nancy Hartfield, this property operates as a working forest. The enacted conservation easement guarantees that this land will remain untouched by housing or commercial ventures, earning recognition from conservation groups for their sustainable management practices.
